title_en: Lin Jinzhang – Enforcement Case of Forced Sale of Real Estate for Refusal to Comply with Court Judgment
keywords_en: enforcement; dispute over private lending; second instance; basic people's court; Fujian Province; natural person; Civil Procedure Law (Trial Implementation); refusal to comply with a judgment; forced sale of real property; enforcement procedure; in favor of the plaintiff; private lending; seizure of house; forced sale
full_text_en:
Lin Jinzhang Refuses to Comply with Court Judgment — Enforcement Case of Compulsory Sale of Property

Enforcement Applicant: Zhang Baozhu, from Chong'an County, Fujian Province.
Enforcement Applicant: Xu Tingying, from Wuyishan City, Fujian Province.
Enforcement Applicant: Liu Shunxing, from Wuyishan City, Fujian Province.
Enforcement Applicant: Zheng Senlin, from Wuyishan City, Fujian Province.
Enforcement Applicant: Tao Hengren, from Wuyishan City, Fujian Province.
Enforcement Respondent: Lin Jinzhang, from Wuyishan City, Fujian Province.

During the period of 1987, Enforcement Respondent Lin Jinzhang borrowed RMB 4,050 from Enforcement Applicant Zhang Baozhu, RMB 4,212 from Xu Tingying, and RMB 33,000 from Liu Shunxing for building a house. Since Lin Jinzhang failed to repay the loans for a long time, Zhang Baozhu, Xu Tingying, and Liu Shunxing filed lawsuits respectively in the Wuyishan People's Court of Fujian Province in March 1989. The court found that the evidence of Lin Jinzhang's borrowing from the enforcement applicants was sufficient, and thus respectively rendered judgments ordering Lin Jinzhang to pay off the debts within 15 days after the judgments took effect. Lin Jinzhang refused to accept the judgments and appealed to the Nanping Intermediate People's Court. The intermediate court rendered a final judgment dismissing Lin Jinzhang's appeal and affirming the original judgments.

Enforcement Respondent Lin Jinzhang borrowed RMB 8,000 from Enforcement Applicant Zheng Senlin and RMB 3,850 from Tao Hengren, and failed to repay them when due. Zheng Senlin and Tao Hengren filed lawsuits respectively in the Wuyishan People's Court. After ascertaining the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, the court conducted mediation, and the parties reached agreements respectively, under which Lin Jinzhang agreed to repay the full amounts on time.

When the enforcement applicants in the above five cases filed their lawsuits with the court, they all applied for preservation of assets. To ensure the smooth enforcement of the judgments and mediation agreements, the Wuyishan People's Court, with the approval of its president, lawfully sealed up one brick-and-wood structured house of Lin Jinzhang that had not yet been completed.

After the judgments and mediation agreements in the above five cases became legally effective, Lin Jinzhang refused to comply with the court's judgments. The enforcement applicants separately applied to the Wuyishan People's Court for enforcement.

The Wuyishan People's Court lawfully decided to enforce the judgments and mediation agreements of the five cases, with a total subject matter of RMB 23,112, in a consolidated manner. Before enforcement, the enforcement officer repeatedly contacted Lin Jinzhang to persuade him to voluntarily comply with the judgments and mediation agreements, but Lin Jinzhang refused to listen. During this period, Lin Jinzhang's husband, Yi Hui, concealed the true facts and registered the house that had been sealed up by the court and registered in Lin Jinzhang's name under his own name (later cancelled), thereby transferring the property rights and evading the law.

On October 26, 1990, the Wuyishan People's Court, in accordance with Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), posted a notice to sell by auction the sealed-up house of Enforcement Respondent Lin Jinzhang.

During this period, the enforcement officer continued to advise Lin Jinzhang to voluntarily comply with the court's judgments and mediation agreements, and, upon his request, granted a certain period of time to allow him to sell the house by himself.

After the deadline expired, Lin Jinzhang still neither complied with the judgments and mediation agreements nor sold the house.

To protect the legitimate rights and interests of the creditors, the Wuyishan People's Court decided to sell the sealed-up house of Lin Jinzhang. On December 22, 1990, the sealed-up house of Lin Jinzhang was sold for RMB 18,600.

Thereafter, the Wuyishan People's Court distributed the proceeds from the sale among the applicants in proportion to the amount of each applicant's claim.
